Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates linear radiolucencies tracking along the mediastinal borders and extending into the neck (subcutaneous emphysema), consistent with pneumomediastinum. In a young patient following an alcoholic binge (suggesting vomiting/retching), this presentation is most characteristic of spontaneous pneumomediastinum caused by alveolar rupture (Macklin effect) rather than esophageal rupture, which typically presents with severe illness and pleural effusion.
